concepts.learning_objective: Identify the ways in which consumers are exploited in the marketplace, such as under-weighing, hidden charges and adulterated or defective goods.
Explain why markets are unfair when a few powerful producers face scattered consumers, and why rules are needed to protect consumers.
Trace how the consumer movement in India arose as a social force in the 1960s and changed who is held responsible for quality.
Describe the role of the 1985 UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection and of Consumers International.
Recall the enactment of the Consumer Protection Act (COPRA) in 1986 and its amendment in 2019.

topics.title: Right to safety and right to be informed

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the right to be protected against goods and services that are hazardous to life and property.
Explain why manufacturers must display particulars such as ingredients, expiry date and MRP on goods.
Describe how the Right to Information Act, 2005 lets citizens obtain information about the functioning of government departments.

topics.title: Right to choice and right to seek redressal

concepts.learning_objective: Recognise situations in which a consumer's right to choose is denied, such as forced tie-in purchases.
Explain the right to seek redressal and compensation against unfair trade practices and exploitation.
Describe how a consumer, individually or as a group, can file and conduct a complaint before a Consumer Commission.

topics.title: Consumer protection councils and the three-tier redressal machinery

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the role of voluntary consumer protection councils and Residents' Welfare Associations in helping consumers.
Identify the district, state and national Consumer Disputes Redressal Commissions and the value of claims each one handles.
Interpret quality marks such as ISI, Agmark, Hallmark and +F, and when certification is mandatory.
Describe how the government spreads consumer awareness, including Departments of Consumer Affairs and National Consumers' Day.
Evaluate the progress made by the consumer movement in India and the role of consumers' active involvement.
Explain why the consumer redressal process has become cumbersome, expensive and time consuming.
State the changes brought in by the 2019 amendment of COPRA, such as online purchases and mediation.
